messages:
alyssa: Heads-up — NimbusPay (ticket #NP-4821) reporting inconsistent rerank scores for identical payloads after the model swap yesterday. Same request produced score deltas > 0.15 in ~10% of calls. Escalating to ops/ML. @devon @tara

devon: Can you paste an example request and the exact model names they hit? Any 429/502/5xx spikes in their timestamps?

alyssa: They called POST /v1/rerank with model 'rwd-rerank-v2' earlier then our routing switched to 'rwd-rerank-v3-quant' during a capacity spike. Sample:
```json
{
  "query": "refund status for order 12345",
  "candidates": ["Order 12345 was refunded on 2026-03-10","Refund pending - contact support","Your refund is processed"],
  "top_k": 3
}
```
They ran ~1000 queries; ~120 showed score delta > 0.1 between calls. Also saw a few 502s and some retries from their client.

tara: Thanks. Tokenization/whitespace differences can produce flips. Did they include any odd unicode or trailing spaces? Also, were they using any sampling params (temperature != 0)?

alyssa: Customer insists payloads were identical, no sampling flags set. They didn't set an idempotency key and did exponential backoff on 502s.

samir: Ops view: I searched request logs for NP-4821 window — three request IDs from their API key at 2026-03-14T22:12Z. For one batch our batch-renderer returned 502 (GPU OOM transient), client retried and the second attempt hit a different routing pool that served v3-quant as fallback due to v2 capacity exhaustion. So same logical request crossed two model variants.

devon: That matches a hypothesis: routing-induced model variant mismatch + quantization differences -> score drift. Also, caching might be primed differently if KV-cache warmed on earlier calls.

tara: I'm running a small repro now: pinned tokenization and greedy decoding, fed the exact payload into both v2 and v3-quant. Early result: mean absolute score difference ~0.12 for the sample set — deterministic seed and no sampling didn't remove the gap.

alyssa: Customer also reported seeing occasional 429s right before the variance spike. They retried immediately (no idempotency). Could duplicate in-flight requests be contributing?

devon: Action items: 1) ops to export raw request+response logs and routing metadata for those request IDs (samir) 2) ml to run a broader eval across our test suite comparing v2/v3-quant on the customer's payloads and provide per-example logits (tara) 3) cs to propose mitigations to customer (alyssa).

samir: Ops updates: extracted logs and saved under /logs/requests/1945679012_nimbus.zip — includes routing decisions, GPU pool metrics, and retry traces. Routing shows automatic fallback to v3-quant during 22:12:09-22:12:15Z spike.

tara: I'll run a reproducibility harness: fix seed, identical batching, same kv-cache state (cold vs warm), and compare raw logits. If diffs persist with cold cache, likely model weight/quantization differences. If diffs only when cache warm -> cache priming ordering bug.

alyssa: For the customer: short-term mitigation request: 1) pin to model 'rwd-rerank-v2@2026-03-10' (we'll share exact version) 2) add an `X-Idempotency-Key` header on retries 3) if they want, offer temporary dedicated capacity for stable routing while we investigate.

devon: Also please note: if client retries cause duplicate concurrently processed requests, and our routing selects different pools, that can create perceived non-determinism. We should consider stronger routing affinity for identical client keys during short windows.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Retention filter set; raw logs retained for 72h at /logs/requests/1945679012_nimbus.zip.

support-bot: Noted — updating ticket NP-4821 with current action items and ETA for ml eval (24h).

alyssa: Great work team — I'll update the customer with the pinning + idempotency steps and share tara's eval once ready. :heart:
